# Electric Theatre Collective - Visual Design System Analysis

## LAYOUT & STRUCTURE
The site uses a modular grid system with flexible spacing. Projects display in a responsive card-based layout that adapts from multi-column desktop to single-column mobile. Content containers have max-widths with centered alignment. The footer uses a two-column structure (London/New York office info) that stacks responsively.

## TYPOGRAPHY
- **Primary font**: "Proxima Nova" across all text elements
- **Font weights**: 400 (regular) appears dominant; 600+ for emphasis
- **Heading hierarchy**: Large display type for main heading "Welcome to Electric Theatre Collective" (appears ~42px based on WordPress preset), smaller weights for project titles
- **Body text**: 16px baseline (--wp--preset--font-size--normal)
- **Labels/UI text**: Smaller sans-serif, maintaining brand consistency

## COLORS
- **Background**: White/neutral (#ffffff primary, #eee secondary)
- **Text**: Dark gray (#2c2d33 for UI elements, #313131 for very-dark-gray preset)
- **Accents**: Purple (#7a00df synced color) used for interactive elements and branding
- **Borders**: Subtle gray/transparent treatments
- **Overlays**: Transparent black/white for hover states

## PROJECT CARDS & IMAGES
Cards showcase thumbnail images (appears to be ~3000px × 1500px contain-intrinsic-size from CSS). Each card displays project title below image. Aspect ratio handling uses contain-intrinsic-size for performance. Images appear as clickable linked blocks with smooth transitions.

## NAVIGATION
**Header nav**: Horizontal menu with 4 main items (Work, Colour, Info, Careers). Mobile: likely hamburger-triggered menu. **Filter system**: Sidebar filters with checkbox/radio inputs, "Reset all" button, category counts in parentheses.

## ANIMATIONS & INTERACTIONS
- Fade/drop animations for UI elements (300ms duration specified)
- Smooth scroll prefetch behavior
- Hover state color changes on navigation links
- Filter functionality with AJAX loading (no page reload)
- "Opens in new window" aria-labels for accessibility

## WHITESPACE
Generous vertical spacing between sections. Card grids have consistent gutters (implied ~2em from WordPress column gap presets). Section padding maintains breathing room around content blocks.

## INTERACTIVE PATTERNS
Filtering with real-time results updates. Featured category pre-selected. Projects load dynamically via AJAX. All external links marked with aria-labels. Button elements have role attributes for accessibility.

## OVERALL AESTHETIC
Clean, minimal professional portfolio. Dark text on light backgrounds prioritizes readability. Purple accent color provides visual identity without overwhelming. Generous whitespace and grid alignment convey premium creative studio positioning. Responsive-first design maintains functionality across devices.

# Electric Theatre Collective Homepage Design Analysis

## 1. Hero Section
The homepage features a **full-screen video player** ("primaryVimeoPlayer") as the primary hero element, displaying rotating video content from their portfolio. The current playing video shows alongside a carousel of additional video thumbnails below.

## 2. Typography & Fonts
The site uses **"proxima-nova"** as the primary font family (enforced via CSS across `.asl_w` and input elements). No explicit Google Fonts links appear in the provided code; "proxima-nova" is loaded as a custom/licensed typeface.

## 3. Color Palette
- **Primary text**: `#2c2d33` (near-black)
- **White**: `#ffffff`
- **Accent/Border**: `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2)` (subtle shadows)
- **UI Elements**: Transparent backgrounds with dark borders
- WordPress theme includes a signature purple: `#7a00df` (brand accent)
- Neutral grays for secondary UI

## 4. Navigation Structure
- **Horizontal menu** with main sections: Work, Colour, Info, Careers
- **Duplicated navigation** (appears twice in DOM—likely mobile + desktop versions)
- Clean, minimal link styling without backgrounds
- Contact information integrated into footer navigation

## 5. Animations & Transitions
- **AOS (Animate on Scroll)** library loaded for scroll-triggered animations
- Video player uses `autoplay=1` with smooth scroll behavior (`behavior: 'smooth'`)
- Flexslider and Slick Slider libraries present for carousel/gallery transitions
- CSS transitions on `.wpc-` elements (filter/product components)

## 6. Footer Structure
Two-column layout containing:
- **Left**: Navigation links + newsletter signup
- **Right**: Office locations (London/New York) with addresses, phone numbers, social media (Instagram/LinkedIn)
- Minimal footer with copyright and policy links

## 7. Scroll-Based Interactions
- **Video carousel switching**: Clicking additional videos scrolls the page 50px above the primary player
- **AOS animations**: Elements animate in on viewport entry
- Prefetch behavior for link anticipation (conservative eagerness)

## 8. Page Structure & Section Order
1. Primary video player (hero)
2. Additional video carousel
3. "You might be interested in" work showcase (grid of featured projects)
4. Navigation/footer contact section
5. Search functionality integrated globally

## 9. Whitespace & Spacing
CSS custom properties define spacing scale (`--wp--preset--spacing--*`):
- Range from `0.44rem` (smallest) to `5.06rem` (largest)
- 2em gap between major columns
- 1.25em gap in post templates
- Consistent rhythm creates breathing room

## 10. Premium/Professional Feel
- **Award-winning studio positioning**: "Multi-award-winning, world-renowned" tagline
- **High-quality video-first design**: Vimeo embedded player suggests professional production
- **Minimalist aesthetic**: Ample whitespace, typography-driven layouts
- **Dual-office presence**: London + New York locations emphasize global scale
- **Curated portfolio display**: Selective project showcase rather than exhaustive listing
- **Institutional design language**: Clean borders, restrained color use, professional imagery

content.text:
Here is my detailed analysis of the Electric Theatre Collective website design system. --- ## Electric Theatre Collective -- Design System Analysis **URL:** https://electrictheatre.tv/electric/work-category-featured --- ### 1. LAYOUT STRUCTURE **Grid System:** - The work/portfolio page uses a **3-column CSS Grid** layout (WordPress `.is-layout-grid` class) - 12 featured projects display across 4 rows of 3 - Grid gap is approximately `0.5em` to `1.25em` between cards (WordPress spacing presets) - The page has a **sidebar + content** split: a filtering sidebar on the left with the project grid occupying the main content area - Content containers are centered with a max-width constraint **Content Flow:** - Page heading at top ("Welcome to Electric Theatre Collective.") - Filter sidebar (left) with category checkboxes - Project grid (right/main) -- 3 columns, flowing left to right, top to bottom - Footer at bottom with two-column office info (London / New York) **Homepage Structure (different from work page):** 1. Full-screen Vimeo video player (hero) 2. Video thumbnail carousel below hero 3. "You might be interested in" featured work grid 4. Footer with contact/offices --- ### 2. TYPOGRAPHY **Font Family:** - **Proxima Nova** is the sole typeface used across the entire site -- a licensed, premium sans-serif. It is not loaded via Google Fonts; it is a custom/Adobe Fonts integration. **Hierarchy:** | Element | Size | Weight | Notes | |---------|------|--------|-------| | Page heading (H2) | ~42px (`--wp--preset--font-size--huge`) | Bold (for "Electric Theatre Collective" portion) | Mixed weight -- "Welcome to" is regular, studio name is bold | | Project titles (H3) | ~16-18px (estimated) | Regular (400) | Clean, understated beneath thumbnails | | Body / base | 16px (`--wp--preset--font-size--normal`) | 400 | Standard body text | | Navigation links | ~16px | 400-500 | Simple, no text-transform | | Filter sidebar labels | ~14-16px | 400 | Category names with count in parentheses | **Key Typographic Choices:** - Single font family throughout -- consistency over variety - No text-transform (no uppercase nav or headings) - Heading uses **mixed weight within a single line** ("Welcome to **Electric Theatre Collective.**") which creates visual interest without additional font sizes - Project titles are deliberately understated -- the image does the heavy lifting --- ### 3. COLOR PALETTE | Role | Value | Usage | |------|-------|-------| | Background | `#ffffff` | Page background, clean white | | Secondary bg | `#eeeeee` | Subtle section differentiation | | Primary text | `#2c2d33` | Near-black, slightly warm -- softer than pure black | | Brand accent | `#7a00df` | Purple -- used for interactive/selected states in filters | | Borders/shadows | `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.2)` | Subtle, transparent black for depth | | Very dark gray | `#313131` | WordPress preset for dark gray text | **Color Strategy:** - Extremely restrained palette -- essentially monochrome (white + near-black) with a single purple accent - The purple `#7a00df` appears only on interactive elements (selected filter states), never as decoration - No gradients, no colored backgrounds on cards, no colored borders - The restraint lets the **project imagery provide all the color** -- the site is a neutral frame for the work --- ### 4. IMAGE / MEDIA PRESENTATION **Project Thumbnails:** - Images are full-width within their grid column - Responsive: `max-width: 100%; height: auto;` - CSS `contain-intrinsic-size` hints at ~3000x1500px source images (2:1 aspect ratio tendency) - No visible border-radius on thumbnails -- sharp rectangular edges - No box-shadow on cards - Images are mixed formats: `.jpg`, `.png`, `.webp` -- no standardized format enforcement **Card Structure (minimal):** ```

[Project Title]

 ``` - No overlay text on images - No category tags, dates, or metadata visible on cards - No description text -- just image + title - The entire card (image + title) is wrapped in a single anchor tag -- the whole area is clickable **Homepage Video:** - Full-screen Vimeo embed as hero (`autoplay=1`) - Additional video thumbnail carousel below using Flexslider/Slick Slider - Clicking a carousel thumbnail scrolls to 50px above the primary player --- ### 5. NAVIGATION **Structure:** - Horizontal menu: **Work | Colour | Info | Careers** - Only 4 items -- extremely minimal - No logo in the nav (the studio name appears in the page content instead) - Two DOM instances of nav (desktop + mobile versions) - No dropdowns, no mega-menus - Clean link styling with no background colors or borders on nav items **Filtering System (Work page only):** - Left sidebar with category filters using checkbox/radio inputs - Categories include: Featured (12), Colour (515), Motion Design (88), Animation (96), Film & Episodic (21), Music Video (73), Automotive (31), Fashion (59), Character Animation (52), Showreels (8), Award Winning (18), Making Of (39), News (30), Archive (643) - AJAX-powered: filters update the grid without page reload - "Reset all" button to clear filters - Selected state uses the purple accent color `#7a00df` --- ### 6. HOW THEY PRESENT WORK **Philosophy: Image-first, metadata-last.** The portfolio grid is deliberately stripped down: - **Only two pieces of information per project:** a thumbnail and a title - No year, no client name separately called out, no role description, no tags - The title itself carries the context: "Nike - The Making of Calling All Athletes" tells you the client (Nike), the project name, and hints at content type - No hover preview, no expand-in-place, no lightbox from the grid - Clicking goes to a dedicated project page **Project Mix (from the 12 featured items):** - Commercial work (Pringles, Sainsbury's, Nike, EA, British Gas, Audible, Genesis) - Entertainment (Netflix, film) - Studio news/culture (team promotions, awards, NY office expansion) - This mix humanizes the studio -- it is not just a reel, it is a living company --- ### 7. WHAT MAKES IT FEEL "CLEAN" **Reduction to essentials:** 1. **Single typeface** (Proxima Nova) -- no font mixing, no decorative type 2. **Monochrome + one accent** -- white background, near-black text, purple only on interactive states 3. **Minimal card anatomy** -- image + title only, no metadata clutter 4. **No decorative elements** -- no lines, dividers, icons, badges, or ornamental graphics 5. **Generous whitespace** -- spacing scale from `0.44rem` to `5.06rem` with consistent rhythm 6. **No box-shadows or borders on cards** -- elements float in white space without visible containers 7. **4-item navigation** -- radical simplicity in information architecture 8. **Consistent grid** -- 3 equal columns, no masonry, no varied sizes 9. **No text on images** -- thumbnails are pure imagery, never overlaid with gradients or text **The "invisible design" principle:** The site disappears so the work can be seen. There is no UI chrome competing with the project imagery. The design system is intentionally boring so the creative work is the only visually interesting thing on the page. --- ### 8. ANIMATION / INTERACTION PATTERNS **Libraries loaded:** - **AOS (Animate on Scroll)** -- scroll-triggered entrance animations for elements - **Flexslider** and **Slick Slider** -- carousel/gallery transitions on the homepage - CSS transitions on filter components (`.wpc-` classes, ~300ms duration) **Observed behaviors:** - Smooth scroll (`behavior: 'smooth'`) when navigating to video player - Prefetch on link hover (speculative loading with `conservative` eagerness) - AJAX filtering with no page reload -- grid updates in place - Video autoplay on homepage hero **What is absent (deliberately):** - No parallax scrolling - No card hover zoom/scale effects - No fade-in stagger on grid items (the AOS library is loaded but used sparingly) - No cursor custom styling - No page transition animations - No loading skeleton screens The interaction design follows the same minimalist philosophy as the visual design -- restrained, functional, never attention-seeking. --- ### 9. SPACING SYSTEM (WordPress Custom Properties) The site uses WordPress's spacing scale as custom properties: ```css --wp--preset--spacing--20: 0.44rem --wp--preset--spacing--30: 0.67rem --wp--preset--spacing--40: 1rem --wp--preset--spacing--50: 1.5rem --wp--preset--spacing--60: 2.25rem --wp--preset--spacing--70: 3.38rem --wp--preset--spacing--80: 5.06rem ``` Grid gaps use `0.5em` (tight) to `2em` (between major columns). The scale follows a roughly 1.5x multiplier progression, creating harmonious proportional relationships. --- ### 10. KEY TAKEAWAYS FOR YOUR PORTFOLIO If you want to apply these principles to josephibrahim.com: 1. **Let the work be the color.** A neutral frame (your dark `#181818` is already doing this well) with restrained accent usage makes project thumbnails pop. 2. **Simplify card anatomy.** Electric Theatre shows only image + title. No tags, no year, no description on the grid view. All detail lives on the project page. 3. **Single typeface consistency.** They use Proxima Nova for everything. Your site uses multiple fonts (Raleway, DIN 2014, Georgia, Open Sans) -- this creates more visual complexity. Consider whether fewer fonts would feel cleaner. 4. **Uniform grid, uniform aspect ratios.** Three equal columns with no size variation. No masonry. No "featured" large cards. Every project gets equal visual weight. 5. **Invisible containers.** No borders, no shadows, no card backgrounds. Items sit in open space. The grid alignment alone creates visual structure. 6. **Minimal navigation.** Four items. No dropdowns. The filtering is a separate, optional sidebar mechanism, not baked into the nav. 7. **Mixed content types in the portfolio.** They interleave commercial work with studio news, awards, and team stories. This makes the studio feel alive rather than being a static reel. 8. **Purple as "interactive-only" accent** is analogous to your amber `#FFB000` -- both are high-saturation accent colors. The key is using it only for interactive affordances (hovers, selected states), never as decoration.
